question: Which element has the highest atomic number and is the heaviest naturally occurring element?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Uranium (U)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Uranium (U)** has the highest atomic number (92) among the naturally occurring elements.
 
• It is also **the heaviest naturally occurring element,** with a high atomic mass.
 
• **Uranium is primarily used as fuel in nuclear reactors **and in the production of nuclear weapons.
 
• Despite its heavy atomic mass, uranium can be found in various minerals such as uraninite.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Uranium was **discovered in 1789 **by German chemist **Martin Heinrich Klaproth**.
 
• It was **named after the planet Uranus**, which had been discovered eight years earlier.
 
• Uranium has several isotopes, i**ncluding Uranium-235 and Uranium-238**, which are used in different nuclear applications.
 
• Due to its radioactive properties, uranium must be handled with care to avoid potential health risks.
 
• Uranium is found in small amounts in rocks, soil, and water, and even in the human body in trace amounts.
